decisions.latin: a fácie (ignis, Dei, ejus, Dei Sínai, Dei Israël)
decisions.why: The Latin says *a fácie* seven times in the psalm (67:2, 3 twice, 5b, 9 twice) and 67:3 sets fire and God side by side under the same phrase. The glossary keeps the face (*diante da face de*, row *fácies*, with *à face de* as its named alternative). *Diante da face de* twice in 67:3 puts the second colon seven syllables over the Latin; *à face de* keeps the face and the echo fire/God at the Latin's length. 67:2, with a verb of flight, keeps *fujam da sua face* (row *a fácie terræ → da face de*).

decisions.why: One verb twice, of smoke and of the enemies. The glossary's *defícere → desfalecer* (open) is a man fainting; smoke does not faint. ἐκλείπει: to fail, give out, vanish. *Desfazer-se* is plain, says the smoke thinning away, and holds the repetition. No *assim* is supplied in the first colon, where the Latin has none (it has *sic* only in the second).

decisions.why: Three places. The glossary row (*conspéctus*, open) gives *à vista de* for predicates and *na presença* where the phrase hangs beside a verb or noun, and warns that *à vista* fails with verbs of motion. 67:4 and 67:5b are joy before God (*exultem na presença de Deus* — *exultem à vista de Deus* sounds like spectators); 67:8 is the going-out of God seen by his people, where *à vista do vosso povo* is exactly DRB's *in the sight of*. Two renderings for one phrase, each where it works.

decisions.why: *exasperáre* is always intransitive in the psalter (65:7, 67:7b, 77:8 — grep), παραπικραίνω, "to embitter, provoke". D27 gave *provocar* to *exacerbáre* and *irritáre* (παροξύνω, God the object); this is another Greek verb and has no object, so it keeps its cognate. *Exasperar* is common Brazilian speech ("isso me exaspera"). Proposed to the glossary as open, for 65:7 and 77:8.

The future is kept.

ἑκούσιον, "freely given". DRB keeps it ("a free rain"). *Uma chuva voluntária* is the Latin's adjective and strange in Portuguese as it is strange in Latin; *generosa* says the gift's quality and leans toward abundance (MS1932 *abundante* is the Hebrew's "rain of plenty").

decisions.why: πῖον, "fat", beside τετυρωμένον, "curdled, cheesed". The glossary gives *pinguis → gordo* (open; *touros gordos*, *os gordos da terra*) and *coaguláre → coalhar* (118:70, milk). Rule 5: concrete images stay concrete. *Monte gordo* is also a common place name in the Portuguese-speaking world, which helps the ear accept it. *Fértil* (MS1932) explains the image.

options.label: monte pingue
options.note: a real Portuguese word for rich/fat, but bookish

decisions.why: *montes coagulátos* can be the object ("why do you suspect curdled mountains?", i.e. imagine other ones — MS1932 *por que pensais em (outros) montes*) or a vocative (DRB "Why suspect, ye curdled mountains?"). ὄρη τετυρωμένα is the same in both cases. Without a comma or a preposition, *por que suspeitais montes coalhados?* keeps both: *suspeitar* + direct object is "surmise". The glossary row *suspicári → recear* (118:39) is another context (a feared reproach).

The glossary gives *étenim → pois*, *nam et → pois também*. In all three places here the Greek is καὶ γάρ and the *et* carries weight: the heavens too (67:9), the Lord too (67:17b), even the unbelievers (67:19b). *Pois também* in all three, one form for the psalm.

The glossary row *currus* (19:8) became *carros de guerra* because a blind reader heard automobiles; it left 67:18 to decide. Here the chariot is God's, among thousands, at Sinai; the ear has less room for a car, but the risk is real. *múltiplex* ("manifold") as a participle, *multiplicado dez mil vezes* (μυριοπλάσιον).

In 67:18 it stands beside *in Sina*, and in 67:25 after *regis mei qui est*: a place both times (DRB "in the holy place … in his sanctuary").

decisions.why: The Greek repeats one root (ᾐχμαλώτευσας αἰχμαλωσίαν), the Latin half-echoes it (*cepísti captivitátem*). *Levastes cativo o cativeiro* is the form Portuguese has for this line (Eph 4:8, *captivam duxit captivitatem* — the Clementine wording not checked here) and says "you took captives" with the Latin's noun (*captívitas → cativeiro*, row). *Cativastes* is "you charmed" in Brazil.

options.label: tomastes cativos
options.note: MS1932 *levaste contigo cativos*; the abstract noun made concrete

decisions.why: *in homínibus* (ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ): "among men" or "in men" (DRB). *Entre os homens* is the Portuguese that can be said; *nos homens* keeps the preposition and sounds broken.

decisions.latin: Étenim non credéntes, * inhabitáre Dóminum Deum
decisions.why: The hardest colon. The Latin reads naturally as an accusative + infinitive after *credéntes*: "even those not believing that the Lord God dwells" — MS1932 *mesmo pelos que não criam que o Senhor Deus habitava*. DRB takes the infinitive as a noun: "for those also that do not believe, the dwelling of the Lord God". The Greek (ἀπειθοῦντες τοῦ κατασκηνῶσαι) is "the disobedient, (so as) to dwell". The draft follows the natural Latin parse and keeps the fragment a fragment, as the Latin is; the imperfect *criam … habitasse* follows the past of 67:19a.

os que não creem * na habitação do Senhor Deus
os que não criam, * para que o Senhor Deus habitasse

forms.inhabitare: para que o Senhor Deus habitasse.

decisions.why: A plural (σωτηρίων). D6 gives *salvação*; the plural *salvações* stands at 27:8 (*salvátio*, row). *O Deus da nossa salvação* is the phrase Portuguese prays; number is grammar (D27, on *sǽculum sǽculi*).

options.label: da nossa salvação
options.note: draft — DRB "the God of our salvation", MS1932 the same

decisions.why: The glossary row *vertex → o alto da cabeça* (7:17) names this verse. With *capílli* beside it, "the crown of the hair": *o alto da cabeleira* keeps both nouns and does not say *cabeça* twice after *cabeças* in the first colon. DRB "the hairy crown".

options.label: o alto da cabeça cabeluda
options.note: the row + an adjective; *cabeluda* is comic

decisions.latin: Ex Basan convértam, * convértam in profúndum maris
decisions.why: *convértam* twice, with no object (ἐπιστρέψω, "I will bring back"; DRB, MS1932 supply "them"). *Farei voltar* is the glossary's causative (*convértere*, 52:7). In the Latin's order the colon ends *De Basã farei voltar* before a verse ending *mar* — an accidental rhyme the Latin does not have (rule 5). Moving *de Basã* after the verb makes the repetition an anaphora in place of the Latin's adjacency; the words and the doubling are all kept.

options.label: Farei voltar de Basã, * farei voltar
De Basã farei voltar, * farei voltar
De Basã voltarei, * voltarei
options.note: intransitive: God himself returns — a possible reading of the bare verb

decisions.latin: lingua canum tuórum ex inimícis, ab ipso
decisions.why: Elliptic in the Latin and the Greek (ἐξ ἐχθρῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ). *ab ipso* can be "from him" or "from the same" (the blood — DRB "be red with the same"). *Dele mesmo* holds both (*dele* = of him / of it, *mesmo* = self / same). No verb is supplied for the second colon; the first colon's *se tinja* governs it, as *intingátur* governs the Latin.

πορεῖαι, "goings, marches" (DRB "goings"). *ingréssus* is a going-in; the noun occurs only here in the psalter (grep). *As vossas entradas* keeps the Latin's noun and MS1932's *entrada (triunfal)*; *passos* belongs to *gressus* (16:5); *procissões* and *cortejo* interpret.
Two nouns in apposition: young women who are drummers. *tamborim* is the usual Portuguese for the biblical hand-drum (and a Brazilian instrument too); *juvéncula* → *moça*, the plain word.
The glossary row *excéssus mentis → fora de mim* (30:23) names this verse. Here of Benjamin: *fora de si*. It holds ecstasy and being beside oneself, as ἐν ἐκστάσει does.

"The beasts of the reed" (τοῦ καλάμου). *Canavial* (MS1932) is a sugar-cane field in Brazil; *caniçal* is the exact word and little known; *juncos* are rushes, the plain word for what grows in a marsh.
Singular in the Latin (τὸν οὐρανὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ). The idiom Portuguese knows is the plural *céu dos céus*, which 148:4 *cæli cælórum* will need. Kept singular here so that the two stay two.

The formula *Benedíctus Dóminus* is verbless in the psalter (*Bendito o Senhor*, D41, 67:20). *Bendito Deus*, without an article, cannot stand verbless in Portuguese; the jussive *seja* is supplied (grammar, D2). DRB "Blessed be God", MS1932 *Bendito seja Deus!*

choices.67:2: *dissipéntur* (people) → *sejam dispersos*: the glossary row *dissipáre* proposes *dispersar* for people (17:15, 34:16); 67:31b *Díssipa gentes* → *Dispersai* the same. *oderunt* present in sense (*odísse*) → *odeiam*. The Latin ends on *a fácie ejus*; Portuguese order puts it before the subject. The verse is Num 10:35.
choices.67:5a: *psalmum dícite* → *entoai um salmo* (row *psállere*, 17:50 *psalmum dicam → entoarei um salmo*). *ascéndit super occásum* → *sobe sobre o poente*: *subir* as 46:6 and 67:19a, 67:33b (the same *ascéndit super*); *occásus → poente* as 49:1.
choices.67:5b: Vós is the plural of the people addressed (*Exsultáte*); God is in the third person, so *dele*, not *sua* (which a Brazilian ear can take as "your"). *turbabúntur* keeps its open subject. The apposition *patris … et júdicis* keeps both genitives. *órphanus → órfão* (row).
choices.67:7b: *in fortitúdine* stands after *os presos*, where it can belong to the bringing-out ("with strength") or to the bound ("bound fast") — the Latin's ambiguity (DRB keeps it too). *edúcere → fazer sair* (row). *simíliter* → *igualmente*.
choices.67:9: *movéri → ser abalado* (row). *distilláre → gotejar*: the concrete drip (DRB "dropped"). *Dei Sínai* read as the Latin has it, "the God of Sinai" (the Greek's τοῦτο Σινα is not followed).
choices.67:10: *infirmáta est* → *enfraqueceu*; *ela* can be the rain or the inheritance, as in the Latin. *perfícere → aperfeiçoar* (row; 67:10 is one of the places it was tried on). *tu vero* → *mas vós*.
choices.67:11: *Animália* → *animais*, the Latin's concrete word (DRB "animals"). *parásti* has no object in the Latin; none supplied. *dulcédo → doçura* (row).
choices.67:14: *pennæ* → *asas* (row, open; the Greek πτέρυγες). The verbless apposition *asas de pomba prateadas* is kept verbless (DRB supplies "you shall be as").
choices.67:15: *discérnit* → *separa* (D42). *cæléstis* as a title, *o Celeste* (DRB "he that is in heaven"). *nive dealbabúntur* → *ficarão brancos de neve* (D44 *dealbári → ficar mais branco*, here without the comparative). *Selmon* as the Latin spells it.
choices.67:17b: The Latin's resumptive *in quo … in eo* is one relative in Portuguese (grammar). *beneplácitum est* → *agradou* (the row *beneplácitum fácere*). *in finem* → *para sempre* (row, D27: perpetuity; εἰς τέλος).
choices.67:18: *in eis* → *entre eles*, with *está* supplied. *Sina* and 67:9 *Sínai* are one place → *Sinai* both.
choices.67:20: *Benedíctus Dóminus* → *Bendito o Senhor* (formula row, D41). *die cotídie* → *dia após dia*. *prósperum iter fáciet nobis* → *nos fará próspero o caminho*; the subject moved to the head of the colon (natural order).
choices.67:21: *Deus salvos faciéndi* → *o Deus que salva*: a gerund as a relative (grammar); *salvum fácere → salvar* (row). The copula supplied, as DRB. *Dómini Dómini* doubled, as the Latin. *éxitus mortis* → *as saídas da morte* (plural, as the Greek; ways out of, or into, death — open as in the Latin).
choices.67:22: *Verúmtamen → Todavia* (row). *confríngere → quebrar* (row). *perambuláre in → andar* (row, the Church sense). *delíctum → falta* (row).
choices.67:24: *tuus*, *tuórum*: the Lord speaks to one (Israel) — *tu*, as D17 (address follows the speaker). *intingátur* → *se tinja*, the Latin's own verb (*tingo*).
choices.67:25: *Rei* capitalised, as *meu Rei e meu Deus* (5:3).
choices.67:27: *In ecclésiis* → *Nas assembleias* (D34). *Deo Dómino* → *a Deus, ao Senhor* (dative repeated in apposition). *de fóntibus Israël* left bare, as the Latin (MS1932 supplies *vós que sois da estirpe de*).
choices.67:29: *Manda … virtúti tuæ* → *Dai ordem … ao vosso poder* (row *mandáre*: *dar ordem* where there is no thing as object; here a dative). *confírma hoc* → *confirmai … isto* (row *confirmáre*: *confirmar* for a thing). *operári → operar* (D43).
choices.67:30: *A templo tuo* → *Do vosso templo*: *de* keeps "from" and lets the causal sense ("because of your temple") be heard. *múnera → dádivas* (row; it names 67:30). Cadence *dádivas* is a proparoxytone, allowed.
choices.67:31a: *increpáre → repreender* (row). *congregátio* (συναγωγή) → *congregação* (D34's Greek test). *ut exclúdant* follows the Latin (positive), not the Greek's τοῦ μὴ ἀποκλεισθῆναι. *probáti argénto* → *provados com a prata* (row *probáre → provar*); the ablative left open (tested like silver, or with silver).
choices.67:31b: *Díssipa gentes* → *Dispersai as nações* (row *dissipáre*, people). *legáti* → *embaixadores* (MS1932). *prævéniet manus ejus Deo* → *adiantará as suas mãos a Deus*: the row's verb *adiantar* used transitively ("put forward"), keeping one family with 67:26 *Adiantaram-se*.
choices.67:33b: *ad Oriéntem* → *para o oriente*; it answers 67:5a *sobre o poente*.
choices.67:34b: *dabit voci suæ vocem virtútis* → *dará à sua voz uma voz de poder*. *super Israël* can belong to *date glóriam* or to *magnificéntia ejus* (the Greek's reading); the second colon is left verbless so both hold. *magnificéntia → magnificência* (row). The Latin's inline *(35)* is not reproduced.
choices.67:36: *Mirábilis → Maravilhoso* (row *mirábilis*). *virtus → poder*, *fortitúdo → força* (rows; kept apart). *plebs → povo* (row).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from the parallels (no DM1962 for this psalm). Hard readings: 67:13 (verbless Rex … dilécti; dative + infinitive), 67:14 (cleros, pallor), 67:15–17 (the fat and curdled mountains; suspicámini with object or vocative), 67:19b (non credéntes inhabitáre), 67:24 (ab ipso), 67:31a (ut exclúdant, against the Greek). The rubric (fit reverentia) in 67:5a translated and kept in parentheses — see decision reverentia. Liturgical uses (grep content/do): 67:6b + 67:36 as the Introit of Pent11-0 (*Deus in loco sancto suo … ipse dabit virtútem*), with 67:2 as its psalm verse; 67:2 also the Introit verse of Pentecost (missa Pasc7-0) and of 01-19; 67:29–30 the Offertory of Pentecost and a Pentecost Office antiphon (*Confírma hoc, Deus*).

Hard checks pass. Soft, all accepted: 67:3 +3 (two *à face de*, the Latin's own repetition); 67:5a +4 (*fazei caminho para aquele*; the rubric in parentheses is not counted) and its rhyme flag *nome / nome*, which is the Latin's *nómini … nomen*; 67:12 +3 after taking *evangelizam* (was +7); 67:13 +5 and +3 (a copula and a supplied *cabe* for a verbless Latin; see decisions rex, speciei); 67:15 +4 and 67:18 +4/+5 (Portuguese articles and *está*; *multiplicado dez mil vezes* for one word *múltiplex*); 67:16b −3 and 67:17b −6 (the resumptive *in eo* dropped: grammar); 67:19a +3 (*levastes cativo o cativeiro*); 67:21 +3 (the copula *são*); 67:26 +8 (*psalléntibus* → *aos que entoavam salmos*, the glossary's *psállere*; no shorter form keeps the psalm); 67:28b +4 (*de* before each tribe); 67:31a +3; 67:33a +3 (*psállite → entoai salmos*, D25). Oxytone cadences throughout (Deus, Israel, Senhor) are allowed.
